author: Claude, from public reporting; a dated snapshot, not a live feed. Ask to refresh it.

themes.name: AI runs out of power
themes.thesis: AI's limit has moved from chips to electricity. The big five cloud companies plan close to $690B of 2026 capex, but transformers take 3 to 5 years to deliver and switchgear is sold out through 2028, so 30-50% of data centers due this year face delays. Whoever can supply power, grid equipment or on-site generation is being paid to remove the bottleneck.
evidence: Hyperscaler 2026 capex plans near $690B (Amazon ~$200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+)
Transformer lead times 3-5 years; switchgear sold out through 2028
US utilities plan about $1.4T of capex, up 27%, much of it for data-center load

tiers.why: Sell the power or the generating equipment directly

tickers.GEV: Gas turbines and grid equipment, the most direct way to add power fast
tickers.CEG: Largest US nuclear fleet; signs long contracts with data centers
tickers.VST: Power producer with nuclear and gas plants in data-center markets
tickers.ETN: Electrical gear inside and around every data center

tiers.why: Build, connect and cool what the first order sells

tickers.PWR: Builds transmission lines and substations; the grid's main contractor
tickers.HUBB: Grid hardware and connectors, with long-dated utility demand
tickers.WMB: Gas pipelines that feed the on-site turbines going up beside data centers
tickers.SO: Utility with some of the largest data-center load additions in the Southeast

tiers.why: Raw materials and specialist labour the buildout cannot do without

tickers.FCX: Copper: every megawatt of grid and data center needs tonnes of it; record price in January
tickers.EME: Electrical and mechanical contractor; skilled electricians are a bottleneck too
tickers.CCJ: Uranium, if nuclear restarts and new reactors follow the power shortage
tickers.BE: Fuel cells, an on-site power option that skips the grid queue

risks: Capex cuts if AI revenue disappoints: the whole chain re-rates together
Many first-order names already price in years of growth
Politics: higher electricity bills could cap what utilities may charge

themes.name: AI's other bottlenecks: memory and networking
themes.thesis: Each new AI chip needs far more high-bandwidth memory (Blackwell B200 carries 192 GB against the H100's 80 GB) and faster links between chips. SK Hynix and Micron have sold out 2026 HBM, and 800G optical transceivers are on 40+ week lead times. Spending shifts from the GPU itself to what surrounds it.
evidence: HBM takes about 23% of DRAM wafer output in 2026, up from about 19%
Micron and SK Hynix 2026 HBM sold out
800G optical transceiver lead times past 40 weeks

tiers.why: Design the AI chips and switches

tickers.AVGO: Custom AI chips for cloud companies and networking silicon

tiers.why: Make the memory and optics every cluster needs more of

tickers.MU: The only US maker of HBM memory, sold out for 2026
tickers.COHR: Optical transceivers and lasers for chip-to-chip links

tiers.why: Equip and test the factories making more memory

tickers.LRCX: Etch and deposition tools; memory makers are its biggest customers
tickers.AMAT: Chip-making equipment across memory and logic
tickers.KLAC: Inspection tools; more complex chips need more of them
tickers.TER: Testers for memory and AI chips

risks: Memory is famously cyclical: shortages turn to gluts when capacity catches up
Export controls on China hit equipment makers
AI spending pause would hit second and third order hardest

themes.name: Global rearmament
themes.thesis: Military spending is set to pass $2.6T in 2026, the fastest sustained rearmament since the Cold War, and the proposed US budget nears $1.5T. Primes win the contracts, but they are capacity-constrained; the suppliers of castings, specialty metals, energetics and electronics are where shortages and pricing power show up.
evidence: Global military spending projected above $2.6T in 2026
Proposed US FY2027 defense spending approaching $1.5T
US metal foundries adding capacity driven by defense demand

tiers.why: Prime contractors that win the programmes
Parts the primes cannot make enough of

tickers.HWM: Engine and airframe castings and fasteners
tickers.TDG: Sole-source aerospace components with pricing power
tickers.HEI: Aerospace and defense electronics and parts
tickers.BWXT: Naval nuclear reactors for submarines and carriers

tiers.why: Specialty materials and new kinds of warfare

tickers.CRS: Specialty alloys for engines and munitions

risks: Budget fights and continuing resolutions delay awards
A peace deal would cool the most crowded names
Fixed-price contracts squeeze primes on cost overruns

themes.name: Reshoring and the industrial buildout
themes.thesis: Factories, chip plants, data centers and grid upgrades are being built in the US at the same time, so leadership this year has rotated to industrials and materials. The second-order winners are the local, hard-to-import inputs: aggregates, steel, contractors and the distributors that keep job sites running.
evidence: Industrials, materials, energy and staples have led the market in 2026 while tech lagged
Market leadership broadening beyond the largest companies in the second half

tiers.why: Equipment that goes into new plants

tickers.CAT: Construction and mining machines, power generation

tickers.MLM: Aggregates: crushed stone can't be shipped far, so local quarries price well
tickers.FIX: Mechanical and electrical contractor for plants and data centers

tiers.why: Supplies and space the buildout keeps buying

tickers.FAST: Fasteners and job-site supplies on a vending model
tickers.GWW: Maintenance and repair supplies for every new plant
tickers.PLD: Warehouses near new factories and ports

risks: Tariff reversals change the maths of building here

themes.name: Obesity drugs go mainstream
themes.thesis: Obesity drugs are already about a $42B market, with roughly $100B more expected by 2029, and pills now make them easier to take and ship. The makers are obvious; the second order is everything needed to produce injectables and pills at that scale, and the third order is how a lighter population changes what it buys.
evidence: Tirzepatide sales: Mounjaro $39.1B and Zepbound $22.9B; Wegovy $18.6B
Oral semaglutide approved late 2025 and rolling out in 2026
Medtech volumes so far not hurt by GLP-1 use

tickers.NVO: Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) and the first pill

tiers.why: Supply the factories, vials and pens

tickers.WST: Injection components used in pens and vials
tickers.TMO: Drug manufacturing services and lab equipment

tiers.why: How spending shifts when people eat less and move more

tickers.PLNT: Gyms: people on the drugs are told to keep muscle
tickers.COST: Bulk grocery buyers shifting toward fresh and protein
tickers.ISRG: Surgery volumes rise as more patients become eligible for procedures

risks: Price cuts as Medicare negotiates and competitors arrive
Pills reduce the need for pens and injection parts
Third-order effects are the least certain

themes.name: Tight oil and gas supply
themes.thesis: Energy is the best sector of 2026, up more than 40% this year on supply worries. When oil and gas stay high, producers turn into cash machines; the second order is the companies that drill and move the product, and the third is shipping, where rates can explode the way container rates did for ZIM.
evidence: Energy up 16.3% in the third quarter and more than 40% this year, the best S&P 500 sector

tickers.CVX: Oil major with a strong balance sheet

tickers.SLB: Oilfield services, paid more when producers spend more
tickers.BKR: Services plus gas turbines and LNG equipment
tickers.VLO: Refiner; wide fuel margins when supply is tight

tiers.why: Ship it: rates spike when supply routes are disrupted

risks: Oil can fall fast if supply worries ease or a recession hits demand
Shipping is the most cyclical of all: ZIM's cash flow collapsed once rates normalised
Producers in a boom may overspend on new supply
